content.thinking:
I'm sorting the outcomes into an order: reject first, then escalate, return, incomplete, and approve last. The "incomplete" outcome is tied to section 2.2, which says a claim can't be approved if any required fact is unknown, and I need to quote that section directly. Next I'm turning to the rules, starting with section 3.1 on rejecting claims submitted 61 or more days late.

I'm working through the rules now: rejecting claims submitted 61 or more days after the earliest expense, rejecting self-approved claims, and escalating claims of $5,000 or more without director sign-off. Then I'm moving on to the return and escalation conditions tied to receipts, alcohol, gifts, and airfare, where one rule about pre-approved business-class airfare seems to conflict with the escalation rule.

I'm deciding whether an approve rule should exist for the pre-approved business-class airfare case, since section 4.5 says it "may be approved" and that would clash with the escalation in 4.4. I'll write the rule as the text states it and let it be shadowed, rather than fixing the conflict. I still need to settle what happens when no rule applies to a claim.

I'm mapping the words a claim might use for each fact's value, such as "business-class" and "business class" both becoming business, and "first-class" becoming first. I'm also checking the lookup for itemised receipts, where "missing" or "has not been attached" both mean no.

I'm thinking about the maps for the cabin and itemised receipt values, with "missing" and "not attached" both meaning no for the receipt. I'm also checking whether any rule needs a fact that isn't available, and I'm wondering whether the "may be approved" wording in 4.5 should be written as an approve rule.

I'm checking the remaining rule details, confirming that the 61-day and $75 thresholds map to fields I already have, and that no extra inputs are needed. I'm also noting which sections define outcomes, the order, and unknown-fact handling, so I can quote the two rules exactly as written.

I'm quoting the rules for the anti-bribery review, airfare review, and the approver check, and noting that a pre-approved business-class airfare may be approved, along with the requirement that any unknown fact blocks approval.

I'm settling on how to handle the 4.5 pre-approved airfare case: I'll write it as an approve rule exactly as the text says, even though it clashes with the escalation in 4.4 and never gets to decide anything. I'm also noting that the SOP never gives a general approve rule, and I'll set the unknown-when-empty collection entry to the one-line-per-receipt wording from section 1.

unknowns.text: A fact that has not been established is unknown, not false. If any fact required by this procedure is unknown, the claim cannot be approved.

lines.unknown_when_empty: which lines (receipts or expenses) the claim has
lines.text: A claim is a list of lines, one per receipt or expense.

rules.text: Claims must be submitted within 60 days of the earliest expense on them. Reject a claim submitted 61 days or more after its earliest expense.
A claim's approver must not be the employee who submitted it. Reject a self-approved claim.
A claim totalling $5,000 or more needs the Finance Director's sign-off. Without it, escalate.
Every line of $75 or more needs an itemised receipt. If a receipt is missing or has not been attached, return the claim.
Alcohol is not reimbursable. Return any claim with a line for alcohol.
A gift to a government official must be reviewed under the anti-bribery policy. Escalate any claim with such a line.
Business-class and first-class airfare must be reviewed. Escalate any claim with such a line.
Business-class airfare pre-approved in writing by the Finance Director may be approved.

sections.note: Defines the five outcomes. Incomplete is used as the unknowns outcome. The sentence 'A claim is a list of lines' grounds the lines collection. The SOP gives no general rule for when a claim is approved.
Sets the unknowns behaviour: a claim with an unknown required fact cannot be approved and is incomplete.

Translated as written. Any line this rule matches also matches 4.4 (escalate), and 2.1 makes escalate govern. So this approve rule can never decide a claim. This conflict between 4.4/4.5 and 2.1 is left for a person to resolve.

findings.title: Pre approved never changes an outcome
